aspects.says: Overloaded constructors delegate with this(...) to one constructor that checks and assigns, so no overload skips a check or a default.
basis: section:Overloaded Constructors Chain with this(...) to One That Checks and Assigns

aspects.says: An object that hands out this from its constructor can be called before its fields are assigned, final ones included, and stays referenced even when the constructor then throws.
basis: section:A Constructor That Hands Out this Lets Others Use a Half-Built Object

aspects.says: A static factory can have a name, return an existing object or a subclass, while new always makes a new object of the named class; callers rely on identity or class only where documented.
basis: section:A Static Factory Can Name, Reuse or Choose the Class of What It Returns

aspects.says: The JLS promises other threads the assigned values of final fields only for references obtained after the constructor finished.
basis: section:A Constructor That Hands Out this Lets Others Use a Half-Built Object
aspects.reason: a data race on an escaped reference can't be produced deterministically in a graded test; the page states it as a hedged side note

aspects.says: Declaring any constructor removes the default no-argument one, so a reflective framework that needs it fails at run time and a subclass without a constructor stops compiling.
basis: section:Declaring Any Constructor Takes Away the Default One

aspects.says: A private constructor that validates and assigns, with a static factory that publishes the finished object, keeps half-built and refused objects out of other code.
basis: section:A Constructor That Hands Out this Lets Others Use a Half-Built Object

aspects.says: On Java 21 a this(...) or super(...) call must be the first statement and its arguments can't read instance fields; arguments are computed by static methods inside the call.
basis: section:Overloaded Constructors Chain with this(...) to One That Checks and Assigns
